title: Psychedelic treatment for headache disorders
abstract: Headache disorders are common neurological conditions with numerous treatment options depending on the specific disorder and the needs of the individual. Psychedelic drugs, such as psilocybin, dimethyltryptamine and lysergic acid diethylamide, have important historical roles in headache medicine and are re-emerging as potential therapeutic options, particularly in cluster headache. The renewed interest in psychedelic treatment for headache is largely attributable to the patient community, who have advocated for their preferred forms of treatment, including psychedelic drugs. Clinical trials in cluster headache and migraine have supported the reported efficacy and safety of psilocybin in the transitional treatment of these disorders, and additional studies of other compounds and modes of treatment are ongoing or on the horizon. In this Perspective, we provide an overview of psychedelic drugs in headache medicine, including historical context, relationship to conventional headache medications, and the limited clinical and scientific evidence to date. Safety, logistical and legal concerns are also discussed to set the stage for future work in the field. The use of psychedelics to treat headache disorders has a long history, and these drugs are re-emerging as potential therapeutic options, particularly in cluster headache. This Perspective provides an overview of psychedelic drugs in headache medicine, including their relationship to conventional headache medications and the limited clinical and scientific evidence of efficacy.
